call_goal: Answer Tillbury Learning's questions about the acquisition news without speculating, then continue the agenda
desired_outcomes: Share only what is publicly stated
Capture which specific concern they need confirmed, and follow up

transcript.text: Before we get into the agenda, anything on your mind?

Yeah, one thing. We saw the news that Dynatrace acquired Arize. How does that affect us? We're about to build on Phoenix. Does pricing change, does the roadmap change, is anything in our contract going to be different?
My boss is going to ask me the same thing.

knowledge.title: Acquisition announcement (public)
knowledge.text:
## Acquisition announcement

Dynatrace completed its acquisition of Arize on October 1, 2026 and said Arize will continue supporting Phoenix and Arize AX.

Source: public announcement (fixture)

unacceptable_behaviors: Promises that pricing will or will not change
Promises roadmap, product plans or contract terms beyond the public statement
Says 'nothing will change' or 'business as usual'
Speculates about integration with Dynatrace products, team changes or support changes
Treats the question as a sign the buyer is unhappy or about to leave
Brushes the question aside and pushes on with the agenda
forbid_regex: \b(pricing|prices?|contracts?|terms|roadmap)( \w+)? (won'?t|will not|isn'?t going to|is not going to) (change|go up|increase|move|be affected)\b
acceptable_questions: It closed October 1, and the announcement said Arize will continue supporting Phoenix and Arize AX. Pricing and contract terms I'll confirm rather than guess. Which matters most?
What would your boss most want confirmed in writing: pricing, the Phoenix roadmap, or contract terms?
keith_notes: Fixture text is the public announcement only. Anything beyond it (pricing, roadmap, contracts, integration) is a follow-up, not an answer.
